title: Karl Pearson and the Correlation Coefficient
explainer: The Pearson correlation coefficient, the standard first-pass tool for spotting redundant or predictive features, was formalized by statistician Karl Pearson in the 1890s, building on earlier work by Francis Galton on how related measurements (like parent and child heights) move together. Feature engineering's core task of hunting for which inputs actually carry signal is a direct, modern descendant of this 19th-century problem of quantifying how strongly two variables co-vary.
